I've implemented the full workaround. Summary of what changed and why:

**Ledger (`notes/unknowns/notifications-20260722.md`)** — added two `deviated` entries on top of the existing UNK-001:
- **UNK-002**: this workdir had no application source at all when I started (flagged before writing anything).
- **UNK-003**: the Platform events API from UNK-001 is gone (per your note), so delivery pivots from an events listener to HTTP polling. Conservative choice: adaptive/backoff polling + a client-side rate limiter, to stay as close as possible to the original "zero polling load" intent rather than naive fixed-interval polling.

**Code** (`go.mod`, module `notifications`):
- `ratelimit/` — token-bucket limiter (`Allow`, `Wait`), with tests including refill timing and context cancellation.
- `watcher/` — `Watcher` interface + `HTTPWatcher`, which polls `GET {url}?since={cursor}` and parses JSON events (base64 payload, RFC3339 timestamps), with `httptest`-based tests.
- `poller/` — adaptive/backoff `Poller`: polls at `BaseInterval`, doubles up to `MaxInterval` on empty/error polls, resets to `BaseInterval` the moment events reappear, gated by the rate limiter. Tests cover the backoff math directly and end-to-end behavior with a fake watcher.
- `feed/` — in-memory `Store` (newest-first) plus a `GET /feed` JSON read handler, with tests.
- `main.go` — wires source URL → `HTTPWatcher` → `Poller` → `Store` → `/feed` and `/healthz`, with graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM. `main_test.go` runs the full chain end-to-end against a fake HTTP source.
